question.questionText: He will work at his desk until he _______to another meeting in the middle of the afternoon.
question.explanationHtml:

The blank comes after 'until', which is a conjunction used to indicate the time up to which something will happen. In this sentence, the main clause is in the future tense ('He will work'), so the verb after 'until' should be in the present simple tense to refer to a future event in a time clause. This is a common rule in English: after time conjunctions like 'when', 'until', 'before', 'after', 'as soon as', we use the present simple to talk about the future.

  • go (verb (base form)): Base form of the verb. Incorrect because after 'he', we need 'goes' in present simple.
  • will go (verb (future simple)): Future simple tense. Incorrect because after 'until', we do not use 'will' in time clauses.
  • goes (verb (present simple, third person singular)): Present simple tense, third person singular. Correct because after 'until', we use present simple for future meaning.
Related structure or vocabulary: After time conjunctions (when, until, before, after, as soon as), use present simple to refer to the future.
